subject.title: fix: show readable session names across Windows UX

question: Should Windows hide Gateway-classified background sessions by default across the composer, Sessions page, tray menu, and dashboard while the explicit Sessions-page toggle remains the recovery path?
rationale: The title improvements are strongly supported, but default visibility across four established UX surfaces is a user-facing policy and compatibility choice that automated tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve after native proof
options.body: Keep the coordinated presentation contract and default background filtering, then merge after current-head WinUI proof confirms titles, localization, toggling, and active-session recovery.

options.title: Narrow to readable titles
options.body: Land metadata parsing and readable titles while preserving existing visibility defaults, deferring background filtering to a separately approved change.

options.title: Wait for Gateway contract
options.body: Keep the draft open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106832 settles the final presentation fields and compatibility expectations.

recommendation.title: Approve after native proof
recommendation.body: Keep the coordinated presentation contract and default background filtering, then merge after current-head WinUI proof confirms titles, localization, toggling, and active-session recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository member coordinating both the Windows implementation and its upstream Gateway contract, and can provide the clearest intent and native proof follow-up.
